question: Within Hebrew and glyph corpora independently, does the same recurring operator exhibit a transferable consequence law that changes with anonymous structural context beyond a context-only baseline and beyond an invariant operator main effect; and, if so, is the pattern of context modulation itself aligned across the two systems without requiring one-to-one operator matching?
claimBoundary: A positive result supports context-conditioned operator effects under the frozen anonymous four-history projector, and if the cross-system gate also passes it supports similarity in where structural context exposes those effects. It does not establish lexical translation, one-to-one Hebrew-glyph identity, historical contact, common authorship, theology, phonetics, English glosses, or that any operator has one invariant standalone meaning.

hebrewSource.tokenIdentity: first numeric lemma component rendered H<number>

representation.state: anonymous equality pattern of the previous four operators, padded by <START>; literal operator identity is excluded from the state label
representation.glyphSegmentation: reuse V19/V15 line-segment projection over the sealed V10 words packet
representation.sharedStateSelection: TRAIN only; state must have at least the frozen minimum event support in both corpora

models.contextOnly: P0(y|S), hierarchically smoothed from TRAIN state outcomes toward the TRAIN global outcome distribution
models.invariantOperator: Pinv(y|S,o) proportional to P0(y|S) times the TRAIN-smoothed operator-wide outcome ratio P(y|o)/P(y); this allows one operator main effect but forces that effect to be invariant across structural states
models.contextConditionedOperator: Pctx(y|S,o), learned from TRAIN (S,o) outcome counts and hierarchically smoothed toward Pinv; pairs below the frozen interaction-support floor collapse exactly to Pinv
models.primaryContrast: log2 Pctx(observed y|S,o) - log2 Pinv(observed y|S,o)
models.null: for each operator, permute its frozen TRAIN interaction-residual blocks across shared structural states while leaving the current-state Pinv distribution fixed; this preserves operator identity, state baseline, residual magnitudes, support pattern, and outcome alphabet while breaking the operator-by-context alignment

contextProfile.definition: for each shared state, average the realized Pctx-vs-Pinv log2 gain within operator first and then across evaluable operators having events in that state
contextProfile.similarity: Pearson correlation of Hebrew and glyph state-gain profiles over the same anonymous structural state labels
contextProfile.null: exactly permute glyph state-profile labels relative to Hebrew when feasible; otherwise use 4096 deterministic permutations

evaluation.fullRule: A within-system context-conditioned effect must pass independently in both holdout and control for that corpus. The strongest cross-system claim additionally requires both corpora to pass both lanes and the cross-system context-profile gate to pass in both lanes. No one-to-one Hebrew-glyph operator pairing is constructed or used anywhere in V20.
